name: Michael A Carusi
current_role: Managing Partner, Lightstone Ventures; General Partner, Advanced Technology Ventures; director, Shoulder Innovations (SI)
profile: Mike Carusi is a life-sciences venture capitalist who joined Advanced Technology Ventures in 1998 and co-founded Lightstone Ventures, investing in biopharma and medical devices. He joined the board of shoulder-implant maker Shoulder Innovations in 2020 with its Series C, and the company's IPO is the source of his listed SEC insider holdings.
interesting_fact: He has appeared on the Forbes Midas List, served on the National Venture Capital Association board and taught as an adjunct professor at Dartmouth's Tuck School of Business.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer (B.S., Lehigh). Before VC he was business-development director at Inhale Therapeutic Systems (now Nektar), and earlier at consultancy The Wilkerson Group he helped open its London and San Francisco offices.
notes: Investor-director, not a founder. The firm site gives no published email; contact goes through the Lightstone website. Aggregator sites disagree on whether his Shoulder Innovations board seat continues in 2026, so check the latest proxy.

name: Gavin Turner
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Mainsail Partners; director, Brilliant Earth Group (BRLT)
profile: Gavin Turner co-founded Austin-based growth-equity firm Mainsail Partners in 2003. It invests in bootstrapped software companies and has nearly $4B in committed capital. Mainsail backed lab-grown and ethical jewelry retailer Brilliant Earth, where he has been a director since 2012 (LLC board) and through its 2021 IPO, so he is an SEC 10% owner as Mainsail's designee.
interesting_fact: Mainsail focuses on founder-owned, bootstrapped software companies that have never raised outside capital, which is unusual among growth-equity firms. It has partnered with 100+ such companies.
deep_cut_fact: He is originally from Cleveland. Before Mainsail he spent seven years at Summit Partners, then joined the senior management of Sirenza Microdevices, a deal he had sourced, which RF Micro Devices later bought for $900M. He skis in winter and sails in summer.
notes: Investor-director. Mainsail's bio page lists the firm's Austin and San Francisco office phone numbers; no published email was found. He serves on the board of the Boys & Girls Club of the Austin Area.

name: Douglas A. Robinson
current_role: Director, Twilio (TWLO); Operating Advisor, Bessemer Venture Partners; former Co-President, Workday (retired)
profile: Doug Robinson spent about 15 years at Workday. He joined in 2010 as a regional sales director when the company had roughly $25M in revenue and rose to EVP of Global Sales and then Co-President (named Nov 2021), running global go-to-market. He has since retired from Workday. He now advises Bessemer Venture Partners and sits on the boards of Twilio and Varicent.
interesting_fact: He joined Workday at about $25M in annual revenue and left with it near $8.9B. Earlier he held sales roles at PeopleSoft and Oracle.
deep_cut_fact: An Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland Browns fan, he planned at 12 to play football at Ohio State. His first job was as a financial analyst at a bank implementing a core banking system, and meeting the bank's software sales executive pulled him into enterprise sales.
notes: Sources date his Workday retirement to late 2024 or 2025. He also advises Ema AI. Bessemer is a possible route to him.

name: L. Dyson Dryden
current_role: Director (some sources say Vice Chairman), Lindblad Expeditions Holdings (LIND); founder, Dryden Capital Management
profile: Dyson Dryden is a former Citigroup tech/media/telecom investment banker who became a serial SPAC executive with Mark Ein's Capitol Acquisition vehicles. As CFO of Capitol II he helped take expedition-cruise operator Lindblad public via a 2015 merger and has sat on its board since 2013. He later led Capitol III (Cision) and Capitol IV (Nesco) as President/CFO.
interesting_fact: Capitol Acquisition Corp. II's 2015 merger brought Lindblad, the National Geographic expedition-cruise partner, to Nasdaq. It was one of the better-known early SPAC deals of the modern era.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in investment banking at BB&T (1998-2000) before Jefferies and Citigroup. He is a director of Washington E-Sports Ventures, formed to buy an Overwatch League team (the Washington Justice) and build esports teams for the Baltimore-Washington-Richmond region.
notes: Low public profile, and his current Lindblad title varies by source, so check the latest proxy. The press contact is for the company, not for him personally. He was formerly Vice Chairman of CDS Logistics Management and a University of Richmond alum (per aggregator profiles).

name: Rafael Santana
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Wabtec (Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies, WAB)
profile: Rafael Santana is a Brazilian-born engineer who spent nearly two decades at GE, running GE Latin America, GE Oil & Gas Turbomachinery Solutions and GE Transportation. He has led Wabtec since July 2019, when it absorbed GE Transportation. He has turned the merged company into a 30,000-employee freight, transit and mining technology group and now also chairs its board.
interesting_fact: He took over Wabtec right as it completed the merger with GE Transportation, the business he had been running at GE, so in effect he came over with the asset to integrate it.
deep_cut_fact: Before GE (joined 2000) he started his career at ExxonMobil and British American Tobacco. He holds an engineering degree from the Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais in Belo Horizonte, and he serves on Pittsburgh's Allegheny Conference on Community Development.
notes: Wabtec's 2026 bio says he previously served on the Travelers board, so that seat has ended. Baker Hughes' annual-meeting site has a profile page for him, which suggests a Baker Hughes board nomination (energy angle); this was not confirmed. The press emails are company contacts, not his own.

name: Matthew B. Klein
current_role: CEO and director, PTC Therapeutics (PTCT); director, ClearPoint Neuro (CLPT)
profile: Dr. Matthew Klein is a surgeon turned biotech executive who has led rare-disease drugmaker PTC Therapeutics since March 2023, succeeding founder Stuart Peltz. He joined PTC in 2019 when it acquired BioElectron, where he had been CMO and then CEO. He then ran clinical development and operations before becoming CEO, and he also sits on ClearPoint Neuro's board.
interesting_fact: He was CEO of BioElectron, the mitochondrial-disease company PTC acquired in 2019. Less than four years later he was running the acquirer, and he also restructured BioElectron while there.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was a burn and plastic surgeon at the University of Washington: associate director of the UW Burn Center at Harborview, director of the plastic surgery residency, and the first holder (2008-2011) of the David and Nancy Auth-WRF Endowed Chair for Restorative Burn Surgery.
notes: Credentials: BA Penn, MD Yale (1997), MS epidemiology UW. The Yale alumni note (https://medicine.yale.edu/news/yale-medicine-magazine/article/1990s--klein) supports the UW surgery background. No dedicated PTC media email was found on the site, so check a recent press release for the current media contact.

name: Alf Melin
profile: Alf Melin is a Swedish finance executive and a roughly 30-year veteran of TechnipFMC and its predecessor FMC Technologies. He became CFO of the subsea and surface energy-technology company in 2021. Before that he held treasury, controller and operating roles, including Treasurer of FMC Technologies, SVP Surface Americas and GM of Fluid Control.
interesting_fact: He is a rare CFO who has also run operating businesses inside the same company: he led its Surface Americas segment and its Fluid Control unit before taking over finance for the whole group.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the company in 1995 and spent his first eight years in a series of postings around the world before moving into senior finance roles. He holds an M.Sc. in Business Administration and Economics from Lund University in Sweden.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy podcast: TechnipFMC is a major subsea oil and gas technology supplier. Low personal profile. The career details come from aggregator profiles because the official TechnipFMC bio page is behind Cloudflare. Confirm the contacts on a recent press release.

name: Timothy Alan Boroughs
current_role: Vice Chairman, Chubb Group and Executive Chairman, Asset Management, Chubb Ltd (CB)
profile: Tim Boroughs is a fixed-income investor who ran Chubb's (formerly ACE's) global investment portfolio as Chief Investment Officer from 2000. In 2025 he moved up to Vice Chairman and Executive Chairman of Asset Management, overseeing Chubb's global asset-management strategy. Earlier he was Director of Fixed Income at Tudor Investment Corp. and spent two decades at Fischer Francis Trees & Watts.
interesting_fact: He spent 21 years (1976-1997) at bond manager Fischer Francis Trees & Watts, rising to Managing Partner and Director of Global Leveraged Investment Activity, then moved to Paul Tudor Jones's Tudor Investment Corp. before joining ACE.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated with highest honors in Finance from Indiana University. He has lectured at the New York Institute of Finance and was a trustee of the American School in London.

public_contacts.value: amy.well@chubb.com (Chubb Group Chief Marketing & Communications Officer, global media contact)

notes: Low public profile; the route is via Chubb corporate communications. The June 2025 promotion was reported by Insurance Journal: https://www.insurancejournal.com/magazines/mag-people/2025/06/16/827425.htm

name: Ariel Cohen
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Navan (formerly TripActions; Nasdaq-listed since Oct 2025)
profile: Israeli-born Ariel Cohen co-founded TripActions with CTO Ilan Twig in 2015. It became Navan, a corporate travel and expense platform, which reached a roughly $9B private valuation and went public on Nasdaq in October 2025. Before that he was an HP product leader and co-founded StreamOnce, which Jive Software acquired.
interesting_fact: Cohen and Twig's first startup, StreamOnce (founded 2012), reached $1M in revenue and was acquired by Jive Software just nine months after founding. Exactly two years after that sale they started TripActions.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Jerusalem and grew up in central Israel. Before founding companies he led product management at Hewlett-Packard, and he earned an MBA from Northwestern's Kellogg School (2008).
notes: A very public, podcast-friendly founder (SaaStr, Grit, HD in HD, 20VC). His X handle is linked from Navan's own blog. Hurun lists the company valuation at $9B, but Navan is now public.

name: Rob Whitehead
current_role: Co-founder, Improbable (leads new venture creation); CEO of Improbable spin-out MSquared
profile: Rob Whitehead co-founded London-based Improbable in 2012 with Cambridge computer-science classmate Herman Narula. They built SpatialOS, a cloud platform for massive simulations and multiplayer games, which drew a $502M SoftBank-led investment. Improbable has since become an AI/web3 venture builder, and Whitehead leads MSquared, its metaverse-interoperability network.
interesting_fact: SoftBank's 2017 $502M investment valued Improbable at over $1B. It was then one of the largest-ever funding rounds for a UK tech startup.
deep_cut_fact: He got into virtual worlds as a teenager before Cambridge, building and selling virtual goods such as weapons and gadgets in Second Life.

public_contacts.value: UKTN podcast appearance: 'What has become of the metaverse' (Aug 2025)

notes: His title has varied over time (CTO, then CPO, now co-founder/MSquared CEO). UK-based. The podcast entry is an appearance on someone else's show, not his own podcast.

name: Nevada Sanchez
current_role: EVP of Engineering, Science Corporation (since July 2026); co-founder, Butterfly Network
profile: Nevada Sanchez co-founded Butterfly Network with Jonathan Rothberg in 2011 and helped develop its ultrasound-on-a-chip, the basis of the handheld Butterfly iQ whole-body scanner. He spent about 15 years there, most recently as SVP and Chief Innovation Officer. In July 2026 he joined Max Hodak's brain-computer-interface company Science Corp. to lead engineering.
interesting_fact: Butterfly's chips integrate about 9,000 silicon ultrasound transducers, each not much bigger than the tip of a human hair, which turns a phone into a whole-body imaging device.
deep_cut_fact: At 22, as a 2011 Hertz Fellow, he deferred his PhD to join Rothberg. Rothberg had asked MIT physicist Max Tegmark for his most brilliant students, and Sanchez had been working in Tegmark's lab. He holds three MIT degrees (EECS S.B., Math S.B., EECS M.Eng.).
notes: Recently moved from Butterfly to Science Corp. (neurotech), so this is a good angle for a deep-tech conversation. The Hertz Foundation is also a possible warm route.

name: Eren Bali
current_role: Executive Chairman, Carbon Health; CTO, Udemy (since Aug 2024, per Wikipedia)
profile: Turkish-born engineer Eren Bali co-founded online-course marketplace Udemy in 2010 and was its founding CEO. In 2015 he founded Carbon Health, a tech-enabled primary and urgent-care chain valued at about $3B at its peak. In August 2024 he handed the Carbon Health CEO role to COO Kerem Ozkay and returned to Udemy as CTO, while staying executive chairman of Carbon Health.
interesting_fact: He is a serial founder of two unicorns in different industries, edtech (Udemy, later public) and healthcare (Carbon Health), and was on Forbes' 30 Under 30 in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Durulova, an apricot-farming village in Malatya, Turkey, and won a silver medal at the 2001 International Mathematical Olympiad. His first startup, the live-stream learning platform KnowBand (2008), never took off, and SpeedDate then recruited him to Silicon Valley as an engineer.
notes: Search budget ran out, so his 2026 status at Udemy was not re-verified; confirm whether he is still CTO. The source is Wikipedia only. No personally published contact was found.

name: Josh Luber
current_role: Co-founder, StockX; co-founder (Chief Vision Officer) of Fanatics Collectibles. 2026 status not re-verified
profile: Philadelphia-born Josh Luber turned his sneaker-data side project Campless into StockX, the 'stock market for things' resale platform. He co-founded it in Detroit in 2015-16 with Dan Gilbert, Greg Schwartz and Chris Kaufman, and it later reached a roughly $4B valuation. He stepped down as CEO in 2019, then co-founded Fanatics Collectibles with Michael Rubin, securing trading-card rights from MLB, NBA and NFLPA and overseeing the purchase of Topps.
interesting_fact: He gave a 2015 TED Talk, 'Why sneakers are a great investment', on the data behind the sneaker resale market, years before StockX became a unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He started Campless, a sneakerhead-data company, while working as an IBM consultant. Before that he briefly practiced as a bankruptcy attorney (he holds a BA, MBA and JD from Emory) and had founded and run three earlier startups.
notes: No personally published contact was verified, and the search budget ran out before his current (2026) role could be checked. Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Luber. The TED bio links @Campless, a legacy account.

name: Travis Rosser
profile: Travis Rosser co-founded Kajabi in Irvine, California in 2010 with software engineer Kenny Rueter. Kajabi is a SaaS platform that lets creators sell online courses, memberships and podcasts. It bootstrapped for nearly a decade before taking Spectrum Equity's minority investment in 2019, then raised $550M at a $2B valuation in 2021, led by Tiger Global. Little public information on Rosser's current activities was found.
interesting_fact: Kajabi traces back to a toy: co-founder Kenny Rueter built a PVC sprinkler toy for his sons, and when he struggled to monetize a how-to video about it on YouTube, the founders built a platform for selling digital content.
notes: Very low profile. Wikipedia confirms him only as co-founder. The search budget ran out, so his current role was not verified and the record is minimal; the company contact is not his own.

name: Jared Grauer
profile: The Hurun Unicorn list names Jared Grauer as a founder of Course Hero, an online study platform valued at $3.6B in 2021 and now owned by the parent Learneo. Wikipedia and Learneo's site credit founding to Andrew Grauer (CEO; founded at Cornell in 2006) and Gregor Carrigan, and neither mentions a Jared Grauer. His identity and role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Course Hero started at Cornell in 2006 as a way for students to share notes and study materials. It became an edtech company valued at $3.6B after a $380M Series C in December 2021.
notes: Possible data error in the Hurun record: the well-known founder is Andrew Grauer. A Jared Grauer could be a relative or early team member, but this is unconfirmed, so do not use it for outreach without checking. The search budget ran out before more could be checked.

name: Abhay Singhal
profile: IIT Kanpur graduate Abhay Singhal co-founded InMobi in 2007 with Naveen Tewari, Mohit Saxena and Amit Gupta. It started as the SMS search engine mKhoj, pivoted to mobile advertising, and in 2011 became India's first unicorn. He now runs InMobi Advertising from the San Francisco Bay Area; the platform reaches over 1.3B people in 190+ countries.
interesting_fact: InMobi began in 2007 as mKhoj ('mobile khoj', Hindi for search), an SMS search service run from a residential apartment in Bangalore. It was renamed partly because 'InMobi' was easier to pronounce outside India.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CEO of InMobi Advertising and Chief Revenue Officer, he served as InMobi's Head of Human Resources, an unusual stint for a technical co-founder. He made the Economic Times 40 Under Forty list in 2018.
notes: He is based in the SF Bay Area. Mobile ad-tech, with InMobi's sister company Glance, is a possible data/AI angle. For press, use InMobi's press page (https://www.inmobi.com/press).
